P1.evidence: Setter notes were referenced but not read back at the open — the prospect actually invited it ("I already heard a few things from Kim, but I would love to hear it from you") and the rep declined, though he did use Kim's note later ("Kim, they mentioned you want to push your mental limits"). The frame was only two-part: "dive into where you're at currently, see what we can help you with. And if we fit perfect, I'll take it through... otherwise I'll put you in the right direction." No 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement taken ("Okay?" / "Awesome. Sounds good") and the open question run.

P2.evidence: Work, training week, current results, diet and energy were all covered properly, and the injury screen was run twice and pushed ("do you feel like you do have somewhat of stiffnesses or pains or anything that are coming up that we need to know about?"). But age and weight only reached the record because the prospect volunteered them ("I'm 200 pounds right now", "I'm 26 years old, dude") and height was never established. Health conditions were never asked — the prescribed Adderall surfaced only because the prospect raised it himself while describing his energy. Sleep was never asked about at all, on a 48-hour-on shift pattern where it is the obvious variable.

P3.evidence: Best phase on the call. Trackable physical goal asked for directly ("do you have somewhat of a physical goal for yourself that is also trackable?"), the bridge past the physical was run hard on the mental voice, and the impact question was pushed until it landed ("How would you impact those other people when you are in that state of yourself?" / "Visualize it, visualize it"). Reflect-back was clean: "From what I was hearing, your big why is actually helping others. Is that correct?" Drove through to future children and a 31-year career. Only the 'something physical you can't do right now' question was left implicit in the job framing.

P4.evidence: The root-cause work was strong. "What do you honestly feel like is missing for you in order to get to everything that we've just talked about?" produced the gap in the prospect's own words: "I just want to have guidance, right? And I need someone, like, constantly checking in." The self-reliance challenge was run properly: "do you honestly feel like if you continue without finding that right guidance... you're actually going to be able to get to those goals?" — answered "to be honest, I don't know." Past attempts were never asked about directly; that he had used trainers and meal plans before only emerged at 00:52 when he volunteered it, after the presentation.

P5.evidence: Consequence question asked in full ("let's say that's the same case in a year from now, how would you look at yourself at that point?") and it produced the strongest material in the call — "I think I'd just start becoming angry... but then I'd start lashing out on other people." Settle check run ("would you be willing to settle for listening to that devil?" / "no, no") and the line in the sand was requested explicitly ("would you also actually be willing to start with that and draw a line in the sand"). The 'why not' follow-up was answered spontaneously rather than asked.

P6.evidence: The one call in this batch where the commitment check genuinely preceded the presentation. The belief check ran at 00:23:24 and the promise sequence at 00:40:29 ("Can you promise those four things to yourself?"), producing an unambiguous yes — "I am promising myself this... I'm ready to go, pretty much. Let's do it" — before a word of the offer was delivered at 00:45:00. The scripted 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' was substituted with the four-promises variant rather than asked as written.

P11.evidence: Payment collection was started properly and immediately — card, name, email, billing country and address were being taken when the recording cuts out at 01:00:24, so completion is unverifiable. Onboarding was offered but not booked: "We booked the onboarding meeting with Trevor, would be either tomorrow or on Thursday" followed by "Then I will also check Trevor's calendar" — no slot was confirmed on the recording. No agreement email was confirmed or signed on the call and no welcome-email / Skool / questionnaire instructions were given, though the rep did say "just going to give you some homework" immediately before the file ends. Scored on what is on the recording; truncation is flagged separately.

notes: Textbook discovery and the only call here where a genuine yes was secured before the offer was presented — that ordering is why it closed in an hour with no objections and it should be the batch's teaching example. Two coaching points regardless of the outcome: the baseline skipped age, height and sleep entirely, and past attempts were never asked about. The serious issue is not adherence — it is that the script has no clinical screen, so disclosed near-syncope at work and prescribed stimulant use passed through discovery as motivation material rather than as a reason to seek clearance.
